anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persistently selects a sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate, leading to inefficient access paths, bad join orders, or inappropriate degrees of parallelism.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level settings for memory, parallelism, checkpointing, and background workers are mis-tuned relative to hardware and workload, creating artificial pressure points that do not reflect real resource limits.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer cannot deliver the read/write bandwidth or IOPS demanded by the workload, driving up latency and queue depth on data, temp, or log volumes.

When all three anomalies co-exist, their symptoms overlap and intensify: queries suddenly flip to table scans or large hash builds, inflating physical I/O; buffer pools and work-memory quotas that are too small or too large cause frequent evictions or spills, further increasing disk traffic; meanwhile the underlying storage is already saturated, so I/O waits soar, checkpoints and log flushes stall, and CPU remains under-utilised despite long response times. The wait-event profile may oscillate between plan-driven CPU spikes and prolonged storage waits, making the root cause appear to shift from the optimizer to the disk subsystem and back.

Causally, a mis-tuned configuration (e.g., reduced cache size or aggressive parallelism) amplifies the impact of a poor plan by forcing more pages to be read and written. The sub-optimal plan in turn floods the storage layer with excess I/O, quickly pushing the device beyond its throughput ceiling. Once storage saturates, latency feedback to the engine becomes erratic, causing further plan invalidations, re-optimisations, or adaptive re-plans that may select even worse strategies. At the same time, prolonged I/O stalls delay checkpoints and background cleanup, which can trigger emergency flushes and additional log pressure, creating a feedback loop that steadily degrades overall database performance.

entry.official_definition: The execution timeout for SELECT statements, in milliseconds.
entry.trigger_condition: A SELECT statement exceeds the configured max_execution_time limit.
entry.workload_impact: The SELECT statement is interrupted by the execution time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
